significance: A sacred fig grown from a cutting of the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, planted in the royal park at Anuradhapura in 288 BCE by King Devanampiya Tissa and protected by later rulers including Vasabha, Sena II and Kirti Sri Rajasinha. Raised on a terrace some 6.5 metres above ground and ringed by walls and companion trees, it draws millions of pilgrims a year.
story: Sri Lankan tradition holds that the southern branch of the original Bodhi tree was carried to the island by the Buddhist nun Sanghamitta, daughter of the emperor Ashoka.
